solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

R050-01.notes: C matches P1 misconception ('simply a translation with pieces missing') reversed by the final line ('deciding what the viewer should keep'). A is the narrator's discarded first-year view (P1 'I imagined the same thing'; P2 'I translated every insult... unreadable'). B: dialect appears in one anecdote only (P2); no claim it is the hardest part. D: supervisor gives one remark; nothing about her long career or films today.

R050-02.notes: P2: 'filled four lines, stayed on screen for less than five seconds, and was... unreadable.' B reversed: 'I translated every insult.' C: the dialect was in the original speech, not the subtitle. D: no joke about a supplier; joke replacement is P4 (wedding/tax pun).

R050-03.notes: 'doesn't need to know what she said... need to know that she won' = convey outcome/force, not content; P5 'You thief!' example confirms. A is the rejected approach. B: no explaining dialect. C reverses 'she won'.

flags.note: C is a plausible overstatement trap; P3 says gestures 'say things that no subtitle could' but never ranks gestures above all spoken dialogue.

R050-04.notes: P3: 'Every word I add pulls the viewer's eyes away from the actors' faces, where much of the meaning lives... a viewer who is busy reading misses them.' A: only one remark from supervisor, not training. C: overstated comparison. D: comedy introduced in P2.

flags.note: B 'survives' is the common-sense lure for 'lives' but fails in context (nothing about meaning persisting).

R050-05.notes: 'the actors' faces, where much of the meaning lives' = where meaning resides/is found. B survives, C grows, D is recorded do not fit a location sense.

flags.note: Answer cue: C echoes 'at the same moment the original audience had' closely.

R050-06.notes: P4: replacement joke 'does the same work in the scene even though it says something else'; in-laws joke 'made the test audience laugh at the same moment.' A contradicts 'says something else.' B: length is not the criterion for jokes. D mistakes the specific example for the criterion.

R050-07.notes: P4: 'Good morning may be enough, because the warmth is in the actor's voice.' B: no claim formal greetings are especially hard. C is the opposite case ('At other times the answer is more'), illustrated by the pun. D: no film-vs-life comparison.

flags.note: Strong word echo in D ('original voices', 'choices') makes it easy to spot.

R050-08.notes: P5: 'A film's audience... hears the actors' real voices beneath every line... anyone watching knows that I have made a choice.' A reversed (subtitles keep fewer words). B: test audience mentioned only for the pun, not as a required review of all choices. C: no comparison of carefulness.

flags.note: Wording defect: 'accepting of them' -- 'them' has no clear plural antecedent in the stem ('what is lost' is singular). Suggest 'accepting of such losses while redefining...'.

R050-09.notes: Final paragraph: 'I still lose things, of course. But I no longer think of my job as deciding what to throw away.' A: P5 'None of this means that subtitles are a lesser kind'; tone not regretful. C contradicts 'I still lose things.' D: viewers noticing is framed positively as honesty (P5), not anxiety.

R050-10.notes: 'I think of it as deciding what the viewer should keep' restates the throw-away vs keep reframe. A: original approach (keep every word) was rejected. B: no new problem introduced. D: the narrator, not viewers, decides ('deciding what the viewer should keep').
